notes:
CROSS-COMPARISON OF THE FOUR VEST POCKET OPTIONS. Laid side by side a customer CAN tell these four apart and no pair is indistinguishable, so no blueprint-match pair finding is raised. The discriminators actually present: vest-lower-slant-flap is the only one with TWO pockets and the only full-front view, its flaps straight-edged; vest-ticket-diamond-flap is the only one whose flap comes to a centre point, mouth level; vest-ticket-slant-besom is flapless and slanted 26 degrees; vest-ticket-right is flapless and level at 9.5.

THE RISK WORTH RECORDING: vest-ticket-right and vest-ticket-slant-besom are both bare, flapless, single mouths on the same panel at the same height, and the ONLY geometric difference in the renders is mouth angle - 9.5 degrees against 26.5. That is a real and readable 17-degree gap, but it is the ENTIRE margin, and the two source drawings for Right Welt and the level Besom sibling are themselves near-identical solid bands, so the welt-versus-besom construction distinction is doing no work in either drawing or render. If a future pass flattens the slant besom at all, the pair collapses.

SET-LEVEL WEAKNESS, not a per-option blueprint miss: the four renders use three different crops (full front, wide three-quarter with a hand in frame, very tight detail, medium three-quarter) and two different cloth colours, so the menu will not read as one system. The tightest crop is also the most accurate image and the widest crop the least legible. NOT measurable on any of the four: vertical placement as a fraction of garment length, because all four crop the shoulders or hem; the button line and button pitch were used as landmarks instead. Absolute depths on the three-quarter views carry perspective error of roughly 10-15 percent, allowed for before scoring.
